title: Fix tenant-level ingestion watermark skew causing missing metrics and broken charts during incidents
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers reported missing time-series data and 'no data' widgets in Console during the 2026-02-26 incident window. Root cause (current hypothesis): a watermark misalignment between the ingestion frontends and the long-term indexer caused mid-window tombstoning of recent metric shards for multi-tenant backends. This manifests as empty charts, truncated series, and trace->metric correlation breaks for affected tenants across Hosted and Dedicated; Private installs require a manual upgrade/migration to pick up the indexer fix. This ticket covers investigation, a safe backfill/repair, and a conservative rollout plan plus private customer migration instructions.
reproduction_steps: Simulate high ingest spikes for tenant T under load test cluster using metrics-producer v2.3
Observe ingestion logs: frontend assigns watermark W1 while indexer persists W2 where W2 < W1 by 2+ minutes
Query Console dashboard time-range that spans the skew window -> charts show missing points and metric TTL tombstone markers
Cross-check trace-based spans emitted during the same timeframe; missing metric annotations appear where indexer tombstoned shard
Run local reindex tool to confirm that rehydrating the missing shard restores dashboard points
acceptance_criteria: Fix merged that normalizes watermark propagation across ingestion frontends and indexer and adds unit/integration tests
Backfill job implemented and tested: rehydrates shards for affected tenants without duplicating series
Canary rollout completed against 5 production tenants (mix of Hosted and Dedicated) with monitoring dashboards showing no new tombstones
Private deployment upgrade docs and migration script published and validated with one pilot customer
Post-rollback/runbook verified and added to incident runbook library
investigation_summary: Initial triage (2026-02-27) found a race in the ingestion coordinator: when the batching gateway experienced brief GC pauses, it emitted a higher watermark to downstream routers while the long-term indexer retained prior commit positions. The mismatch was exacerbated by a recently deployed optimization that reduced the heartbeat frequency between gateway and indexer. Reproduced in staging by adding artificial pause to batch-gateway; confirmed rehydration by reindexing tombstoned shards restored console charts. Metrics show ~12 tenants affected during the incident window; two support escalations (ACME and FinElixir) reported product impact. Proposed fix: 1) add transactional watermark handshake between gateway->router->indexer, 2) increase heartbeat safety, 3) add observability metric watermark_lag_seconds, and 4) implement conservative backfill job with tenant-scoped rate limits.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Backfill may spike indexer load -> Mitigation: tenant-scoped rate-limit and backoff, monitoring thresholds with auto-throttle
Risk: Private customers on older indexer version cannot run rehydrate -> Mitigation: publish migration script and offer assisted upgrade window
Risk: Fix increases end-to-end latency marginally -> Mitigation: measure percentiles in canary and rollback knob in deployment config
rollback_plan: If canary shows >2% increase in 99th percentile token latency or increases tombstones elsewhere, rollback handshake change and revert heartbeat to previous value; pause backfill and run corrective rate-limiter adjustments. Incident channel and console-maintainers oncall to coordinate.
notes: Design decision: handshake uses existing gRPC control channel to avoid adding new RPC surface; agreed with infra lead Liam O'Connor
Follow-up: add alerts for aggregate tenant watermark_lag_seconds > 120s in prod and map to runbook step 3
Follow-up: schedule post-deploy retrospective with Observability SWAT to validate dashboards and tracing correlations
